value.rationale: The source treats Shannon and Holevo curves as the information-theoretic temperature limits of classical and quantum decoding. The final theorem extracts a natural structural invariant of those curves: near rate one quantum decoding has an unbounded multiplicative inverse-temperature advantage, whereas near rate zero the advantage is only additively unbounded and relatively vanishing. This clarifies the resource geometry beyond finite-rate percentage comparisons and is not a parameter renaming or table recomputation.
